author: Rebecca J Hogue, hosted by Sam Illingworth
contribution: Short writing sample; request a limited number of improvement areas; human makes the edits and can reject advice.
basis: First-person use with a before/after example and explanation of the prompt constraint.
limits: Reported learning is not measured unaided transfer. Separate the exercise from platform privacy claims.
title: How Can Writers Use AI Ethically?

author: Sam Illingworth; co-editor Alyssa Fu Ward; named creative contributors
contribution: Illingworth keeps a disputed poetic choice. Joshua Sherman describes revising his own lyrics after debate and building a checklist he uses without AI.
basis: Named first-person accounts with concrete creative decisions; Sherman records as First Radio On.
limits: Self-reports, not independent evaluations. Other contributors use different boundaries. Do not attribute every account to the editor or treat reuse as legal clearance.
coverage: Main body and contribution headings inspected; images not assessed
title: How Creatives Are Actually Using AI (And What They Refuse to Let It Do)

author: Ethan Mollick
focus: Test AI on the actual job
contribution: Use realistic tasks, repeated attempts and expert assessment to learn where a model works for a particular job.
basis: Worked model comparisons and research examples.
limits: Model rankings age quickly. Better assisted output does not establish stronger human judgment or learning.
coverage: Expanded body and evaluation examples inspected
title: Giving your AI a Job Interview

author: Hamel Husain and Shreya Shankar, interviewed by Lenny Rachitsky
contribution: Inspect real traces, have a domain expert record failures, group errors, and compare automated judgments against human labels.
basis: Detailed consulting/practitioner account using the Nurture Boss case; explicit example of missing domain knowledge.
limits: Reliability of an AI system is the immediate outcome. Human capability growth remains unmeasured. ID653 repeats this transcript body.
coverage: Expanded timestamped passages; not the entire interview
title: Why AI evals are the hottest new skill for product builders | Hamel Husain & Shreya Shankar

author: Hilary Gridley, interviewed by Lenny Rachitsky
focus: Generate practice questions in the learner's work context
contribution: Her Aristotle GPT generates LSAT-style reasoning questions in a product context; the learner answers before seeing an explanation.
basis: First-person description of a tool she built and uses.
limits: Answer keys need expert checking. No measured unaided transfer; business judgment is broader than solving a logic question.
coverage: Expanded surrounding turns; not the entire interview
title: How to build a team that can “take a punch” | Hilary Gridley (Head of Core Product, Whoop)

author: Cal Newport
focus: Check whether AI helps the real bottleneck
contribution: Identify valuable work and its bottleneck; judge tools by that work and protect time for it.
basis: Explicit author proposal illustrated by a reported researcher interview.
limits: No validation of this routine. Supporting aggregate productivity claims were not independently checked.
title: Avoiding Digital Productivity Traps

author: Melchior Tamisier-Fayard, Theodoros Evgeniou, Anne-Laure Fayard
focus: Design team routines that preserve independent reasoning
contribution: Compare the Prompt with Me challenge, AI-free discussion, parallel human/AI work and interfaces that expose underlying evidence.
basis: Research synthesis and named organizational cases, including AstraZeneca and With Company.
limits: Trace cases to original accounts before making causal claims. Local export has no byline; authors/date verified in NOVA catalog. Its six printed pages differ from the catalog edition's ten pages; this alone does not establish missing content.
coverage: All six extracted PDF pages inspected
path: raw/inbox/Practical/Random/Design AI Systems That Actually Strengthen Human Reasoning.pdf
title: Design AI Systems That Actually Strengthen Human Reasoning

author: Sam Illingworth
focus: State your thinking before the prompt
locator: [ch.21] Conclusion, One thing to try this week
contribution: Write what you think and what you need to know before asking AI; compare what changes and notice when your own answer was enough.
basis: Explicit exercise proposed in the book.
limits: Benefits are proposed, not demonstrated. Book and newsletter are not independent corroboration. Chapter marker is the EPUB document number.
coverage: Section-level screen across book; conclusion read in full
title: Slow AI (book)

author: Annie Duke, interviewed by Lenny Rachitsky
focus: Independent input and advance stopping criteria
contribution: Collect judgments and reasons independently before discussion; attach future actions to signals that would justify stopping.
basis: Explicit decision practices and examples of use, including structured forms.
limits: AI adaptation would be an inference, not a tested method established by this interview.
coverage: Expanded timestamped passages; not the entire interview
title: This will make you a better decision maker | Annie Duke (Thinking In Bets, former pro poker player)

author: Laura O'Driscoll, hosted by Sam Illingworth
focus: Question the assumptions in a belief or draft
contribution: State a belief, invite clarifying questions, and examine assumptions; contributor also checks drafts for sweeping claims before publishing.
basis: Concrete prompt plus first-person repeated use and an example question.
limits: The model cannot reliably diagnose where a belief came from. Discomfort or reduced certainty is not evidence of improved accuracy; factual premises still need external checking.
title: Use AI to Examine Your Beliefs and Reveal Hidden Assumptions

author: J Hong, hosted by Sam Illingworth
focus: Check claimed memories against external records
contribution: A model claimed a dream and a source file existed; the contributor searched actual records. Preserve this as a failure case for prompt-only checking.
basis: First-person failure account with a named checking action.
limits: The advertised self-check prompt did not stop fabrication. No proof that a false memory was implanted; the underlying dream remains unresolved.
title: Is your AI overwriting your memory?

author: Khaled Ahmed, hosted by Sam Illingworth
contribution: Compare generated material against a reference and ask separately about unsupported statements and missing information.
basis: Contributor's compiler-history worked example with reported errors and gaps.
limits: A model reviewing its own output is not independent verification. Absence from one reference need not mean falsehood. Reported error counts and speed are not validated.
coverage: Expanded procedure and worked example inspected
title: Stop Trusting Your Intuition When Evaluating AI

author: Sabrina Ramonov
focus: Interview for context, then challenge the proposal
contribution: Build context through questions, then ask for counterarguments, blind spots and risks when considering an idea.
basis: Commercial practitioner tutorial with an example exchange.
limits: Promotional intelligence and savings claims are unsupported. Challenge is not truth; check factual premises and retain the decision.
coverage: Earlier passage check plus expanded tutorial; not every line
title: How to Get Ahead of 99% of People

author: Ruben Hassid
contribution: State the problem before prompting, set stopping boundaries, and compare activity against actual goals.
basis: Explicit proposed rules and a prioritization prompt.
limits: Fixed task ratios are heuristics. Strong psychological/research claims are unverified; an editorial placeholder reduces confidence. Arguing with the model is not a success measure.
title: Workaholic.

author: John Nosta
locator: [ch.25] Chapter 7, Sequence Matters; Protect the Baseline
contribution: Make an initial sketch before AI and alternate assisted and unaided work to notice what the person can still do alone.
basis: Author proposals supported by interpretation of research; source is already integrated in the KB.
limits: Recheck the cited MIT and clinical studies before repeating causal deskilling claims. Reuse existing source/workbench; do not ingest the duplicate EPUB. Consider overlap with stronger existing evidence.
coverage: Section-level screen across book; expanded Chapter 7 reading, with a small output gap
title: The Borrowed Mind (book)
